title: DCdetector: Dual Attention Contrastive Representation Learning for Time Series Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Time series anomaly detection aims to identify deviant samples from the normal sample distribution, requiring representations that effectively discriminate anomalies.

gap.claim: Reconstruction-based methods dominate, but learning representations with anomalies can cause large abnormal losses that hurt performance.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes DCdetector, a multi-scale dual attention contrastive representation learning model for time series anomaly detection.
DCdetector uses a dual attention asymmetric design to create a permutated environment and pure contrastive loss to learn a permutation-invariant representation with strong discrimination abilities.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the dual attention asymmetric design as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art results on multiple time series anomaly detection benchmark datasets.
The authors report that the code is publicly available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Time series anomaly detection is important across many applications.
The task requires representations that distinguish anomalous samples from the normal distribution.
Existing reconstruction-based approaches may suffer from abnormal losses during representation learning.
The paper proposes multi-scale dual attention contrastive representation learning with an asymmetric design and pure contrastive loss.
The authors report state-of-the-art benchmark results and public code availability.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, metrics, baselines, or numerical results.

The abstract does not report limitations, computational costs, or failure cases.
